paragraphs.en: The Saw-Horse, finding himself alive, rolled his knotty eyes around, taking in his new surroundings. Unable to turn his head, he kept circling without seeing his body. His stiff legs, lacking knee-joints, caused him to bump into Jack Pumpkinhead, sending the latter tumbling onto the roadside moss.
paragraphs.zh: 马蹄木马发现自己竟然还活着，四处转动着它那疙瘩般的眼睛，打量起四周的新环境。由于无法转动头部，他只能不停地绕圈走动，却始终看不见自己的身体。他的腿僵硬无比，没有膝关节，因此不断撞到了杰克南瓜头身上，结果把后者摔在了路边的苔藓上。

paragraphs.en: Tip shouted "Whoa!" but the Saw-Horse ignored him, stepping on Tip's foot and making the boy dance away in pain. Jack, now sitting up, remarked that the horse couldn't hear them.
paragraphs.zh: 蒂普喊了一声“吁！”但木马置若罔闻，踩到了蒂普的脚，疼得男孩跳了起来。杰克此时坐起身来，说道，那匹木马根本听不见他们的话。

paragraphs.en: Tip angrily insisted he had shouted loudly enough. Jack explained that the Saw-Horse had no ears.
paragraphs.zh: 蒂普生气地说他已经喊得够大声了。杰克解释说木马并没有耳朵。

paragraphs.en: Realizing this, Tip wondered how to stop the prancing creature. Suddenly, the Saw-Horse stopped, having concluded it couldn't see its own body. It approached Tip, who patted its head and coaxed "Good boy!"
paragraphs.zh: 意识到这一点，Tip 想起了如何制止这匹尥蹶子的马。突然间，那匹锯齿马停了下来，它认为自己看不见自己的身体。它走近了 Tip，Tip 用手拍了拍它的头，并轻声说道：“好家伙！”

paragraphs.en: The Saw-Horse then examined Jack Pumpkinhead with bulging eyes.
paragraphs.zh: 马蹄随后用瞪大的眼睛仔细打量着南瓜头杰克。

paragraphs.en: Tip decided he needed a halter for the Saw-Horse. From his pocket, he found strong cord, which he tied around the horse's neck and fastened to a tree. Despite the effort, the Saw-Horse easily snapped the string but didn't try to run away.
paragraphs.zh: 提普决定给木马戴上笼头。他从口袋里掏出一根结实的绳子，绕在木马脖子上，并固定在一棵树上。尽管费了一番力气，木马轻松地扯断了绳索，但却没有尝试逃跑。

paragraphs.en: "Stronger than I thought," Tip noted, "and rather obstinate."
paragraphs.zh: “比我想的还要坚强，而且相当固执。”蒂普remarked。

paragraphs.en: Jack suggested, "Why don’t you give him some ears? Then you can tell him what to do."
paragraphs.zh: 杰克建议：“要不你给他弄一对耳朵？这样你可以告诉他该怎么做。”

paragraphs.en: "That's a great idea!" exclaimed Tip. "How did you come up with it?"
paragraphs.zh: “这真是个好主意！”蒂普脱口而出，“你是怎么想到的？”

paragraphs.en: "I didn't think of it," replied the Pumpkinhead. "It’s simple and easy."
paragraphs.zh: “我没有想到这一点，”南瓜头回答，“这很简单易行。”

paragraphs.en: Tip then took out his knife and carved some ears from tree bark.
paragraphs.zh: 蒂普随后拿出小刀，在树皮上刻出了几只耳朵。

paragraphs.en: "Let's not make them too big," he said as he whittled, "or our horse might turn into a donkey."
paragraphs.zh: “别做得太大了，”他在削木头时说道，“否则我们的马可能会变成驴。”

paragraphs.en: "Why would that happen?" asked Jack.
paragraphs.zh: “怎么会发生这样的事？”杰克问道。

paragraphs.en: "A horse has bigger ears than a man; a donkey has even bigger ones," explained Tip.
paragraphs.zh: “马的耳朵比人的大；驴的耳朵更大。”蒂普解释道。

paragraphs.en: "If my ears were longer, would I be a horse?" inquired Jack.
paragraphs.zh: “如果我的耳朵再长一些，我就变成马了吗？”杰克问道。

paragraphs.en: "Friend," said Tip seriously, "you'll always be a Pumpkinhead no matter how big your ears are."
paragraphs.zh: “朋友，”蒂普庄重地说，“无论你的耳朵有多大，你永远都只是一个南瓜头。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I think I get it," nodded Jack.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我想我明白了。”杰克点了点头。

paragraphs.en: "If you do, that's amazing," remarked the boy. "But there’s no harm in thinking you understand. The ears should be ready now.
paragraphs.zh: “如果你真这么想，那太好了，”男孩说道，“不过，不妨想想自己理解了也没关系。现在耳朵应该已经准备好了。”

paragraphs.en: Will you hold the horse while I stick them on?"
paragraphs.zh: “你来牵着马，我来钉上这些钉子？”

paragraphs.en: "Certainly, if you help me up," said Jack.
paragraphs.zh: “当然，如果你帮我一把,”杰克说道。

paragraphs.en: Tip helped him stand, and they approached the Saw-Horse. Tip held its head as the boy made two holes with his knife-blade and inserted the ears.
paragraphs.zh: 蒂普帮他站稳了身子，然后他们走近了木马。男孩用刀片在木马上开了两个孔，蒂普则扶住了它的头部，将耳朵插了进去。

paragraphs.en: "They make him look very handsome," commented Jack admiringly.
paragraphs.zh: “他看起来非常英俊。”杰克赞叹道。

paragraphs.en: But these words startled the horse, which bounded forward, knocking Tip to one side and Jack to the other. The horse then continued to run, apparently frightened by the sound of its own footsteps.
paragraphs.zh: 但这些话却让马儿大吃一惊，它猛地向前一跃，把提普撞到了一边，杰克又撞到了另一边。随后，马儿继续飞奔起来，显然被自己脚步声吓着了。

paragraphs.en: "Whoa!" shouted Tip as he got up. "Whoa!
paragraphs.zh: “住手！”蒂普站起身喊道，“住手！”

paragraphs.en: You idiot, whoa!"
paragraphs.zh: 你这个笨蛋，天哪！

paragraphs.en: The Saw-Horse seemed unresponsive but stepped into a gopher hole, tumbling head-over-heels and landing on its back, flailing its legs wildly.
paragraphs.zh: 锯马似乎没有反应，却径自走进了一个土拨鼠洞，翻了个跟头，四脚朝天地摔在地上，四肢乱蹬。

paragraphs.en: "You're a nice sort of a horse," exclaimed Tip. "Why didn't you stop when I yelled 'whoa?'"
paragraphs.zh: “你这匹马还蛮不错的嘛，”蒂普脱口而出，“为什么你不在我喊‘停住’的时候停下来呢？”

paragraphs.en: "Does 'whoa' mean to stop?" asked the Saw-Horse in surprise as it rolled its eyes upward at the boy.
paragraphs.zh: “‘谁啊’是叫停的意思吗？”小马驹惊讶地问道，它向上翻了翻眼睛看着男孩。

paragraphs.en: "To be sure; unless you step over it," answered Tip.
paragraphs.zh: “当然；除非你跨过去,”蒂普回答道。

paragraphs.en: "This is such a strange place," the creature exclaimed, sounding amazed. "What am I doing here anyway?"
paragraphs.zh: “这里真是个奇怪的地方，”那生物惊讶地喊道，“我怎么会在这里？”

paragraphs.en: The boy explained, "I've brought you to life. Just stay still for a moment while I set you upright." The Saw-Horse, confused, asked, "How many sides do I have?"
paragraphs.zh: 男孩解释说：“我已经让你复活了。你先别动，让我把你扶起来。”马蹄人困惑地问道：“我有多少面？”

paragraphs.en: Tip replied briefly, "Several," and instructed the horse to keep its legs still.
paragraphs.zh: 蒂普简短地回答：“几匹。”然后吩咐马儿保持四肢不动。

paragraphs.en: After several attempts, Tip rolled the Saw-Horse over and set it upright. The creature sighed, saying, "Ah, I seem all right now."
paragraphs.zh: 经过几次尝试，蒂普终于把木马翻了过来，并让它站了起来。那匹木马叹了口气，说道：“啊，我现在感觉好多了。”

paragraphs.en: Tip examined the Saw-Horse and found one ear broken. He decided to make a new one. Returning with Jack Pumpkinhead, who was struggling to stand, Tip whittled out a new ear and attached it to the horse's head.
paragraphs.zh: 提普检查了木马，发现一只耳朵坏了。他决定给它做一个新的。带着摇摇欲站的杰克南瓜头一起回来后，提普削出了一个新的耳朵，并把它固定在木马的头上。

paragraphs.en: "Whoa!" means stop; "Get-Up!" means walk forward; "Trot!"
paragraphs.zh: “吁！”表示停止；“起立！”表示前进；“小跑！”

paragraphs.en: means go as fast as you can," instructed Tip to the Saw-Horse. The horse agreed, saying, "I believe I do."
paragraphs.zh: “你尽全力跑吧。”蒂普对马驹吩咐道。马驹点了点头，回答说：“我相信我能做到。”

paragraphs.en: Tip explained that Jack would ride on the horse’s back for the journey to the Emerald City. The horse offered, "Anything that suits you suits me." With caution, Tip helped Jack mount the horse.
paragraphs.zh: 蒂普解释说，杰克将会骑在马上前往翡翠城。马儿提议道：“适合你的就是适合我的。”蒂普小心翼翼地帮助杰克上了马背。

paragraphs.en: "Hold on tight," he warned, "or you may fall off and crack your pumpkin head." Jack shuddered at the thought. "What shall I hold on to?"
paragraphs.zh: “抓紧了，”他警告道，“否则你可能会摔下来，撞破你的南瓜脑袋。”杰克一想到这个就打了个寒战。“我该抓住什么呢？”

paragraphs.en: he asked.
paragraphs.zh: 他问道。

paragraphs.en: Tip hesitated before suggesting, "Why, hold on to his ears." The Saw-Horse protested, "Don't do that! For then I can't hear."
paragraphs.zh: 蒂普犹豫了一下，才建议道：“喂，抓住他的耳朵。”木马抗议道：“别那样做！否则我就听不见了。”

paragraphs.en: Realizing this was a problem, Tip went into the woods and cut a short limb from a young tree. He sharpened one end, dug a hole behind the horse's head, and hammered the post firmly into its back.
paragraphs.zh: 意识到这是一大难题，蒂普走进森林，砍下了一根小树的短枝。他将一端削尖，在马头后面挖了个洞，然后用力将木桩钉在了马背上。

paragraphs.en: "Stop! Stop!" shouted the horse, as it felt jarring.
paragraphs.zh: “停！停！”马儿感受到车身晃动，脱口喊道。

paragraphs.en: "Does it hurt?" asked the boy. The Saw-Horse replied, "Not exactly hurt, but it makes me quite nervous to be jarred."
paragraphs.zh: “疼吗？”男孩问道。木马回答说：“倒也不完全是疼，但被颠簸得这么厉害让我挺紧张的。”

paragraphs.en: Tip encouraged Jack: "It's all over now. Hold tight to this post." Jack gripped it firmly.
paragraphs.zh: 蒂普鼓励杰克：“一切都结束了。紧紧抓住这根柱子。”杰克牢牢地握住了它。

paragraphs.en: "Get up," said Tip to the Saw-Horse, which obediently walked forward, rocking from side to side as it lifted its feet.
paragraphs.zh: “起来吧，”蒂普对小马驹说道。小马驹乖乖地向前走去，抬起脚时身体还左右摇晃着。

paragraphs.en: Tip began whistling contentedly. The horse asked, "What does that mean?" "Just ignore it," replied Tip.
paragraphs.zh: 蒂普开始愉快地吹起了口哨。马问道：“这什么意思？”蒂普回答说：“就当没听见。”

paragraphs.en: "I'm just happy."
paragraphs.zh: “我高兴极了。”

paragraphs.en: Jack commented, "If I could whistle, I'd do the same. I fear I lack some skills."
paragraphs.zh: 杰克感慨道：“要是我会吹口哨，我也能这么做。我恐怕缺少一些技巧。”

paragraphs.en: They continued for a while until the path widened into a yellow-brick road with a sign: "NINE MILES TO THE EMERALD CITY." It was getting dark, so Tip decided to camp by the roadside.
paragraphs.zh: 他们走了好一阵子，直到小径逐渐拓宽成一条铺着黄色砖块的道路，并立着一块牌子：“九英里到翡翠城。”天色渐晚，蒂普决定在路边扎营。

paragraphs.en: He led the Saw-Horse to a grassy mound and helped Jack alight. "I'll lay you on the ground for the night," said Tip. "You'll be safer that way."
paragraphs.zh: 他把锯马带到一片草地上，帮助杰克下了马。“今晚我让你躺在地上吧。”蒂普说道，“那样你会更安全一些。”

paragraphs.en: "How about me?" asked the Saw-Horse. "It won't hurt you to stand," replied Tip, "and you can watch us."
paragraphs.zh: “那我呢？”木马问道。“站一会儿对你也没坏处，”蒂普回答，“你可以看着我们。”

paragraphs.en: Tip then stretched out beside Jack and fell asleep quickly from exhaustion.
paragraphs.zh: 蒂普随后躺在杰克旁边，疲惫不堪地很快进入了梦乡。
